paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Peter writes to believers who feel like foreigners and exiles, and he tells them to live in a way that makes people see their good deeds and glorify God (1 Peter 2:11-12). Submitting to the king, to governors and even to unreasonable masters isn't about being a doormat. It's about doing it "for the Lord's sake" (1 Peter 2:13), and Peter says it's God's will that by doing good you silence the ignorance of foolish men (1 Peter 2:15). I know the comeback feels better, but good living lasts longer than a clever line.

Now, freedom. Peter says to live in freedom, but not to use it as a cover-up for evil, and to live as servants of God (1 Peter 2:16). So what do you do when doing right still costs you? Peter says if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, "this is commendable before God" (1 Peter 2:20). Nobody's asking you to enjoy it, friend. God sees it, and He calls it commendable.

And you don't carry this alone, because Christ went first. He left you an example, and when they heaped abuse on Him, He did not retaliate, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly (1 Peter 2:21, 23). He also bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness (1 Peter 2:24). You were like sheep going astray, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls (1 Peter 2:25). I thank Him every day for finding me, so follow His footsteps, baker, and know that He's walking right there with you.
